2610.35854.tldr: FL4N adds a lightweight ControlNet-style dynamic encoder to a frozen pretrained static latent NVS model, learning temporal residuals from monocular video. It reports state-of-the-art 4D novel view synthesis across eight benchmarks, rendering faster than Gaussian-based feed-forward methods.
2610.35854.why: Directly relevant to feed-forward 4D reconstruction. It shows a latent, primitive-free alternative to 4D Gaussians and a way to reuse static priors under scarce dynamic data.
2610.35854.reason: Feed-forward 4D novel view synthesis, squarely on dynamic reconstruction interests
2610.35854.qn: Sensible residual-on-frozen-prior idea; evidence broad, but only the intro was seen.
2610.35854.abs: 4D novel view synthesis (NVS) aims to render dynamic scenes across viewpoints and timestamps, which requires jointly inferring 3D structure and temporal dynamics. Existing monocular feed-forward methods often rely on explicit 4D Gaussian representations, which are prone to temporal inconsistency and severe rendering artifacts. We present FL4N, the first feed-forward latent 4D NVS model. Instead of relying on explicit 4D primitives, FL4N encodes a 4D scene prior into a unified latent representation across space and time. Our core insight is that learning temporal dynamics as residuals on top of a pretrained static latent prior enables effective 4D modeling with limited dynamic training data. To this end, we introduce a lightweight dynamic encoder that leverages static scene features to disentangle object motion from camera-induced parallax. Trained solely with an image synthesis objective, FL4N achieves state-of-the-art 4D NVS quality while rendering in real time. Its learned latent representation generalizes to real-world videos and disentangles viewpoint from time.

2610.35706.tldr: Triage is a training-free attention method for video DiTs that assigns each tile to skip (block means), skim (NVFP4), or refine (NVFP4 residual), chosen by a router. A fused Blackwell FP4 kernel gives up to 2.32x end-to-end speedup and 0.3-3.0 dB higher PSNR than baselines.
2610.35706.why: Directly targets efficient video DiT inference by unifying sparse and low-bit attention. Useful for accelerating Wan2.2/HunyuanVideo-based world model pipelines, though it requires Blackwell FP4 hardware.
2610.35706.reason: Efficient sparse/low-precision attention for video DiTs, directly core
2610.35706.qn: Principled marginal-gain routing with fused kernel, strong baselines; Blackwell-specific and PSNR-only evidence visible.
2610.35706.abs: Attention over tens of thousands of visual tokens dominates the inference of video diffusion transformers (DiTs). Existing methods reduce this cost through sparsity, low precision, or both, but use a single precision for all kept tiles. We observe that the output error introduced by approximation varies widely across tiles. Many tiles can be skipped with little error, others must be computed but gain little beyond low precision, and a few retain substantial error even at low precision. We present Triage, a training-free attention method that assigns each tile one of three approximation tiers: skipping it by replacing it with its block means, skimming it in NVFP4, or refining it with NVFP4 residual correction. A lightweight router predicts each tile's error under each tier from block statistics and moves a tile to a more accurate tier only when the predicted error reduction justifies the extra compute, with a single price setting this trade-off. A fused kernel executes all three tiers in a single pass on the FP4 tensor cores of RTX Blackwell GPUs. Across Wan2.2, HunyuanVideo, and LTX-2.5, Triage accelerates end-to-end generation by up to 2.32x over dense FlashAttention, and in each of five settings it runs faster than every baseline while reaching 0.3-3.0 dB higher PSNR than the highest-PSNR baseline.

2610.34233.tldr: BoundedGS trains 3DGS region by region, releasing rasterization caches after each region's gradient is collected, with candidate-indexed projection and compact gradients. Rendering working set stays ~1.07 GiB from 1K to 16K; on 5K scenes it drops 82% with similar quality and slightly faster training.
2610.34233.why: Memory-efficient high-resolution 3DGS training matters for optimization-based 3D reconstruction pipelines. Constant-memory regional backward passes could be reused for high-res 4D or dense-supervision settings.
2610.34233.reason: Memory-efficient high-resolution 3DGS training; directly on core topic
2610.34233.qn: Solid systems engineering with clear memory evidence, but incremental and limited baseline comparisons.
2610.34233.abs: High-resolution 3D Gaussian Splatting training increases pixel and Gaussian-tile intersection counts, expanding rasterization caches that coexist with projection and gradient state at peak memory. A complete-view update aggregates gradients across the view; each region's forward and backward caches can be released after its contribution is collected. BoundedGS separates rasterization and projection backward passes and bounds the active local rasterization working set according to its measured load. Candidate-indexed projection and compact gradient storage address the view-level peaks exposed by this change, while CPU-assisted structure rebuilding and bounded image supply manage resources outside rendering. In a resolution sweep at a fixed count of about 6M Gaussians, the measured rendering working set stays within 1.073-1.077 GiB from 1K to 16K; at 11K, a warm pass takes 19.79 seconds versus 21.76 for full-frame execution. Across five native 5K outdoor scenes, full training reduces the mean rendering working set from 9.97 to 1.76 GiB (82.3%), retains similar reconstruction quality, and shortens training time from 36.7 to 33.9 minutes. Project page: https://xiaobin2001.github.io/BoundedGS-Web/

2610.35529.tldr: WorldPager places int4-quantized KV memory of Matrix-Game 2.0 in a GPU/DRAM/NVMe hierarchy with pose-extrapolated prefetching, plus training-free position extension, producing 37.5 minutes of video on one RTX 4090 at ~9.5 fps with zero stalls.
2610.35529.why: Memory-augmented world models with camera-pose retrieval are central to your interests; this offers systems-level efficiency for long-horizon consistent generation, including KV quantization and prefetching on consumer hardware.
2610.35529.reason: Long-horizon world model memory, KV caching across NVMe tiers, camera-pose prefetch; core interests
2610.35529.qn: Solid systems characterization and honest limits, but narrow single-model evaluation and modest quality evidence.
2610.35529.abs: Interactive world models keep the KV of past chunks as retrieval memory so that revisited places stay consistent. On a single consumer machine (one RTX 4090, 32 GiB of host memory, one NVMe SSD), long sessions with such memory hit two walls. The first is capacity: the KV of Matrix-Game 2.0 exhausts host memory after 45 seconds of video in bf16 and after 2.8 minutes in int4. The second is the model's positional horizon of 4.3 minutes. We show that this memory is capacity-bound rather than bandwidth-bound and that its access set is known before compute, because the camera pose is an input. An analytical model built on these observations predicts spill points to within one chunk and classifies zero versus non-zero stalls correctly on held-out configurations. Guided by it, WorldPager stores int4 KV in a GPU/DRAM/NVMe hierarchy instead of recomputing it, prefetches each chunk's memory from the extrapolated pose, never waits on a miss, and writes back in the background; to our knowledge, it is the first to place the KV memory of an interactive world model on an NVMe tier with zero-stall prefetching. With training-free position handling, it generates 37.5 minutes of video continuously with zero stalls and constant host memory, at about 9.5 frames per second. On a sealed test set, int4 storage shows no measurable quality loss; on long-gap revisits it lowers image quality by about one MUSIQ point.

2610.33566.tldr: DTTD post-trains camera-controlled video models for large-step trajectories: the frozen model generates dense-trajectory teacher videos, which together with geometry rewards rank sparse-trajectory candidates for offline preference optimization (LoRA) with a cumulative curriculum.
2610.33566.why: Directly targets camera-controlled video world models with 3D consistency and large camera motion. The self-distillation and geometry-reward preference tuning recipe could be reused in your video DiT work.
2610.33566.reason: Camera-controlled video world models with 3D consistency and self-distillation; directly core.
2610.33566.qn: Sensible self-teacher idea; the intro offers no quantitative evidence or baseline comparisons.
2610.33566.abs: Video world models are expected to generate videos that accurately follow specified camera trajectories while maintaining consistent 3D structures. However, existing models are predominantly trained on densely sampled videos with small inter-frame camera motions. When applied to sparse, large step trajectories, they often produce frozen frames, inaccurate camera motion, and severe geometric drift. We attribute this degradation to a mismatch between the gradual viewpoint transitions seen during training and the large viewpoint changes required at inference time. To address this problem, we propose Dense Trajectory Teacher Distillation (DTTD), a post-training framework that transfers a model's generation capability from dense trajectories to large camera motions. Given a sparse trajectory, DTTD interpolates additional camera poses to construct a dense trajectory covering the same path. The frozen base model then generates reliable teacher videos along this familiar dense trajectory, and pose aligned teacher observations are used to evaluate candidate videos generated under the original sparse trajectory. In this way, the model serves as its own generation teacher, requiring neither additional video data nor a stronger external video generator. We further combine dense teacher supervision with geometry aware rewards that assess cross frame consistency and camera trajectory following, and use the resulting preferences for offline preference optimization. To stably expand the model's motion range, we introduce a cumulative curriculum that progressively incorporates larger motion steps while retaining simpler trajectories to reduce capability forgetting.

2610.34235.tldr: ParetoGS builds nested pruned 3DGS anchors with persistent identities, stores their parameter residuals in a compact atlas, and interpolates between anchors to decode any Gaussian count. It beats CLOD-3DGS, MGS, FlexGS-imp and NanoGS-imp at matched budgets across 13 scenes.
2610.34235.why: Relevant to efficient 3DGS and level-of-detail rendering. Budget-adaptive decoding from a single asset is useful for scalable reconstruction, though it is not video diffusion.
2610.34235.reason: Continuous-budget 3DGS representation; directly on core topic
2610.34235.qn: Sensible design with broad comparisons, but incremental and evaluated against a narrow set of scalable-3DGS baselines.
2610.34235.abs: Scalable 3D Gaussian Splatting allows one scene representation to serve different Gaussian-count budgets, yet its quality-budget curve may lag behind models optimized separately for each budget. Reducing the number of Gaussians changes both the selected members and the reconstruction tasks carried by the survivors; parameters inherited from a high-budget model may fit a low-budget representation poorly. We propose ParetoGS, which describes member changes and parameter evolution with a small set of adapted budget anchors and decodes intermediate budgets without separate optimization at every requested count. ParetoGS alternates pruning and fixed-member adaptation to build nested anchors with persistent identities, and encodes their parameter changes relative to the full model in a compact residual atlas. At decoding, it interpolates the states of shared members and gradually introduces the rendering contributions of new members, connecting sparse anchors into a continuous-budget representation. Across 13 scenes, ParetoGS attains better average PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS with fewer Gaussians than the compared prefix methods at 10% of each method's own full model. From a shared full model, it also outperforms FlexGS-imp at its trained 1%, 5%, and 10% budgets and NanoGS-imp at the 1% and 0.1% budgets. On Garden, its non-anchor quality approaches an empirical reference from independently optimized GNS models at higher retention ratios and exceeds it at some lower-budget points. Across 13 scenes, encoding reduces mean additional state from 390.0 to 85.7 MB with an average PSNR change of 0.01 dB. Project page: https://xiaobin2001.github.io/ParetoGS-Web/

2610.35347.tldr: CVTSplat uses an SDF-adaptive centroidal Voronoi tessellation for multi-view surface reconstruction, with custom GPU kNN, approximate Voronoi construction and a rasterizer for small cells; it is 5-10x faster at Voronoi building and trains in ~2.5 minutes on DTU/BlendedMVS with competitive accuracy.
2610.35347.why: Offers an efficient, adaptive alternative to 3DGS for surface reconstruction, with a fast differentiable rasterization pipeline relevant to optimization-based 3D reconstruction and efficiency work.
2610.35347.reason: Multi-view surface reconstruction competing with Gaussian splatting methods, efficient training.
2610.35347.qn: Solid engineering and speedups; accuracy only 'competitive', evidence limited to DTU/BlendedMVS.
2610.35347.abs: Voronoi tessellations have recently emerged as an adaptive, space-partitioning discretization for shape and appearance reconstruction from multi-view images. However, the irregular cells they produce make the repeated reconstruction of the tessellation during optimization costly. We therefore explore adaptive centroidal Voronoi tessellations (CVTs), which extend standard CVTs with non-uniform cell sizes while preserving the regular, well-shaped cells that make them efficient to compute. In CVTSplat, cell size is modulated by the evolving signed distance field, concentrating sites near the zero level set while keeping cells nearly centroidal. This regularity lets us specialize the whole pipeline, with GPU algorithms for nearest-neighbor queries and approximate Voronoi construction, and a rasterizer tailored to small, nearly isotropic cells. Our Voronoi construction is 5 to 10 times faster than general-purpose alternatives in this regime. On DTU and BlendedMVS, CVTSplat reaches geometric accuracy competitive with the best Gaussian-splatting surface methods while training in about 2.5 minutes on a single GPU.

2610.35224.tldr: Per-Gaussian motion modeled as piecewise cubic Bézier splines with learnable non-uniform segment boundaries and G1 continuity via reflected control points. Claims better reconstruction on highly dynamic scenes (N3V, Google Immersive, synthetic) and competitive results on general scenes.
2610.35224.why: Directly relevant to 4D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction; adaptive temporal capacity per Gaussian is a compact, network-free trajectory representation that could inform dynamic scene modeling.
2610.35224.reason: Adaptive Bezier trajectories for dynamic 4D Gaussian Splatting
2610.35224.qn: Sensible incremental idea; evidence only competitive on standard benchmarks, gains on niche dynamic scenes.
2610.35224.abs: We present GaussianSpline, a dynamic 4D Gaussian Splatting method that models per-Gaussian motion using adaptive, non-uniform piecewise cubic B\'ezier splines. Unlike approaches based on global deformations, fixed-order polynomials, or uniformly parameterized splines, GaussianSpline jointly learns the B\'ezier control points and the temporal partition of each Gaussian's trajectory. This adaptive representation allocates greater temporal capacity to highly dynamic regions while maintaining compact trajectories for near-static regions, enabling high-fidelity reconstruction of complex and rapidly changing motion. To jointly achieve globally smooth motion and local adaptivity, we enforce $G^1$ continuity between consecutive B\'ezier segments using a reflection-based constraint on their control points. This produces smooth, fully differentiable trajectories while preserving the flexibility of non-uniform temporal parameterization. Experiments on the Neural 3D Video benchmark, the Google Immersive dataset, as well as on synthetic scenes demonstrate that GaussianSpline substantially improves reconstruction quality in scenes with highly non-uniform and challenging dynamics, while maintaining competitive performance on general dynamic scenes compared with state-of-the-art 4D Gaussian Splatting methods.

2610.34344.tldr: Replaces heuristic 3DGS densification with a first-variation score from differentiating the multiview loss w.r.t. per-Gaussian auxiliary mass coordinates, used to pick birth and death sites inside 3DGS-MCMC; reports SOTA quality, especially under small Gaussian budgets.
2610.34344.why: Offers a principled densification/pruning criterion for 3DGS optimization, with gains under tight primitive budgets, which is relevant to efficient 3D reconstruction.
2610.34344.reason: Improves 3DGS-MCMC density control, directly on core 3D Gaussian splatting interest.
2610.34344.qn: Neat principled idea, but incremental over 3DGS-MCMC and the intro gives little evidence.
2610.34344.abs: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has become a standard representation for real-time novel-view synthesis. Yet, its quality-efficiency trade-off still relies heavily on adaptive density control. Existing cloning, splitting, and pruning rules use proxy signals, such as position gradients, opacity, and image-space error. Although effective in practice, these signals do not directly answer the structural question behind density control: where should new Gaussians be allocated to reduce the multi-view reconstruction loss, and which existing primitives can be pruned with minimal penalty. To address this, we propose first-variation birth-death control for 3DGS, a principled approach that replaces heuristic structural decisions with a variational score derived from the reconstruction loss. At each structural update, we freeze the current Gaussian population, attach auxiliary mass coordinates to each primitive, and differentiate the multiview loss with respect to these coordinates. We demonstrate that this score is a coordinate of the first variation of the Splat Regression Model, giving a rigorous local descent surrogate for birth-death moves: high-score Gaussians are selected as birth sites, while low-score, low-opacity Gaussians are selected for removal. Across standard 3DGS benchmarks, integrating this score into 3DGS-MCMC yields state-of-the-art reconstruction quality and outperforms existing methods, delivering the most significant gains under tight Gaussian budgets. Ultimately, our work provides compelling evidence that gradient-based variational metrics offer a principled alternative to proxy heuristics in 3DGS.

2610.35756.reason: Text-guided 3DGS editing using video diffusion priors for multi-view consistency
2610.35756.qn: Creative video-diffusion-based 3DGS editing; evidence only summarized as stronger than baselines
2610.35756.abs: Recent advancements in text-guided 3D editing, particularly with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), have shown promise but still lag behind the flexibility of 2D editing tools. Existing methods face a critical trade-off between preserving multi-view consistency and allowing structural modifications. Image-based editors can also struggle to apply the intended edit to objects viewed from unusual angles. To address these limitations, we introduce VidEdit3D, a framework that reformulates 3D scene editing as a trajectory-based video editing task. By drawing a parallel between camera movement in static 3D scenes and temporal dynamics in video, we leverage the robust spatiotemporal priors of pre-trained Video Diffusion Models (VDMs) to encourage semantic and structural coherence across views. Specifically, we propose Trajectory-Guided Rendering (TGR) to select informative keyframes and construct smooth video clips aligned with VDM input requirements. To propagate edits from an anchor view to these clips, we develop Flow-Aligned Video Editing (FAVE), a training-free framework incorporating an Editing Consistency Guidance (ECG) mechanism. ECG contrasts source and edited image conditions at a shared latent state, using scheduled source-image amplification to strengthen adherence to the edited reference while maintaining original scene context. Finally, we introduce Region-Selective 3DGS Refinement (RS-GS) to strictly confine geometric and appearance updates to target primitives, reducing background attribute leakage. Experiments demonstrate stronger instruction alignment and better multi-view consistency than the baselines.

2610.33589.tldr: Mix Forcing jointly trains a 14B video diffusion model with teacher forcing and bidirectional attention (MoBA) plus chunk-wise prompts, then applies CD and DMD for a four-step causal generator. It reports SOTA quality and one-hour rollouts without degradation.
2610.33589.why: Directly relevant to autoregressive video world models with camera control and few-step distillation of video DiTs; the causal pre-training recipe could inform your efficient inference and long-horizon work.
2610.33589.reason: Causal autoregressive video world model with distillation to few steps; highly relevant.
2610.33589.qn: Sensible recipe and large scale, but internal benchmark and unclear isolated ablations in the intro.
2610.33589.abs: While interactive video world models require autoregressive generation, directly adapting pretrained bidirectional video diffusion models into autoregressive ones with teacher forcing can disrupt their visual priors and degrade autoregressive generation quality. In this paper, we introduce Mix Forcing, a causal pre-training paradigm for interactive video world models, implemented with the Mixture-of-Bidirectional-and-Autoregressive (MoBA) attention. Mix Forcing jointly trains a video diffusion model with both teacher forcing and bidirectional training, yielding a strong causal initialization for few-step post-training. In self-attention, Mix Forcing leverages teacher forcing to learn causal next-chunk prediction for autoregressive rollout, while using bidirectional attention to preserve pretrained visual priors. To support online text interaction, Mix Forcing further adopts a chunk-wise cross-attention design that conditions each video chunk on a shared environment prompt and its own local prompt, without exposing future instructions to the current chunk. Following causal pre-training on a 14B image-to-video model, we apply consistency and distribution matching distillation to obtain a four-step autoregressive generator. Experiments on our internal benchmark and public benchmarks, including WBench and SANA-WM-Bench, show that our model achieves state-of-the-art visual quality and timely event following with precise camera control. Notably, our model supports high-fidelity long-horizon generation without quality degradation even over one-hour rollouts. Project page is here: https://zelingao98.github.io/mixforcing

2610.35806.tldr: Linear probes on frozen VGGT features predict relative-pose failure on held-out HardMatch categories with ROC-AUC 93.5%, versus 79.7% for VGGT's own confidence. The signal emerges in the view-fusing layers, transfers to PhotoTourism and ScanNet-1500, and appears in π³ too.
2610.35806.why: VGGT-style feed-forward reconstruction is core to your work; a cheap failure detector from internal features helps with reliability, abstention, and understanding where cross-view geometry forms in the network.
2610.35806.reason: Uncertainty estimation for feed-forward VGGT pose predictions; directly on core 3D reconstruction
2610.35806.qn: Clean probing study with layer analysis; limited to pose failures, mostly one benchmark.
2610.35806.abs: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models such as VGGT regress cameras and geometry in a single forward pass, but they report no uncertainty for the camera poses they predict: an incorrect relative pose looks no different from a correct one. We ask whether the frozen model nonetheless knows when its pose is wrong. On HardMatch, a benchmark of 1,000 deliberately difficult image pairs on which VGGT fails on 35% of pairs, a linear probe on VGGT's frozen features predicts pose failure on held-out categories with ROC-AUC 93.5%, compared with 79.7% for VGGT's own point-map confidence and 77.7% for a classifier trained on all of VGGT's outputs. The probe catches failures VGGT is confident about, lets a downstream system abstain on the pairs it distrusts, and transfers without retraining to rotation failures on PhotoTourism and ScanNet-1500, beyond what co-visibility explains. This knowledge is absent from the per-image encoder: it is computed partway through the layers that fuse the two views, and the same holds for a second model, $\pi^3$. In essence, we find that VGGT knows more about its own failures than it reports.

2610.34632.tldr: RIDE-Splat separates windshield reflections from driving scenes in 3DGS by modeling the reflection as one shared signed image fixed in image coordinates, then refitting a clean 3DGS in a second pass. Beats 3DGS, DC-Gaussian and RobustSplat by up to 3.59 dB PSNR.
2610.34632.why: Relevant to 3DGS reconstruction from in-the-wild driving video; the camera-attached versus world-consistent decomposition is a useful prior, and the paired-traversal benchmark could be reused.
2610.34632.reason: Reflection-free 3DGS reconstruction from driving video; directly in 3D reconstruction
2610.34632.qn: Sensible, simple decomposition with a new paired real benchmark; limited to a static dominant reflection.
2610.34632.abs: Driving video captured through a windshield violates the world-space consistency assumed by 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS): the road scene exhibits parallax while cabin reflections remain attached to the camera, causing standard 3DGS to embed reflected content into the reconstructed scene. We introduce RIDE-Splat, a pipeline for reflection-free 3D reconstruction from posed driving video without clean images, reflection masks, or pretrained networks. RIDE-Splat assigns world-consistent transmission through the windshield to a 3DGS scene and the dominant camera-attached reflection to one shared, signed RGB image. It builds the clean reconstruction in two passes. First, it learns the 3D geometry and the signed reflection image, representing both added radiance and transmission attenuation. Then, it uses the reflection-removed training images to fit a clean 3DGS model. At inference, the reflection image is discarded, preserving the standard 3DGS rendering path. We also introduce the RIDE-Splat Dataset, the first 3D reconstruction benchmark for reflection removal from driving video -- with real driving scenes, physical windshield reflections in training views, and separately captured non-reflective evaluation images. Across the RIDE-Splat Dataset, XLD, and Wayve, RIDE-Splat outperforms 3DGS, DC-Gaussian, and RobustSplat on all nine aggregate metrics, improving PSNR by up to 3.59 dB and reducing LPIPS by up to 0.0876. We achieve the highest metrics in 38 out of 42 per-scene comparisons and removes windshield reflections that remain visible in the baselines while preserving the transmitted scene.

2610.35594.tldr: Adds a self-supervised representation loss to DMD video distillation: a student sees a noisier input and predicts an EMA teacher's internal features. This reduces flickering and improves spatial and motion quality in bidirectional and causal few-step students.
2610.35594.why: Directly relevant to few-step distillation of video diffusion transformers, including causal autoregressive students used in world models. It is a cheap add-on to DMD with no external encoder.
2610.35594.reason: Few-step video diffusion distillation, directly on efficient video DiT interests
2610.35594.qn: Sensible, cheap idea; the introduction gives no quantitative evidence or baselines, and novelty over Self-Flow-style methods is unclear.
2610.35594.abs: Few-step distillation is essential for deploying modern video diffusion models. Among existing approaches, Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) has emerged as a highly promising paradigm by achieving strong output-space fidelity without adversarial training, while remaining flexible across various student architectures. We observe, however, that DMD fundamentally relies on an output-space objective, lacking explicit regularization on the model's internal representations. As the distillation step count aggressively shrinks, this output-only supervision becomes insufficient, causing the distilled student to degrade in both fine-grained spatial structures and coherent temporal dynamics. To address this limitation, we introduce Self Flow Forcing (SF$^2$), which incorporates a predictive representation loss into the DMD framework without altering its output objective. By providing the student and an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) teacher with heterogeneous noise levels, we establish an information asymmetry. This formulation forces the student to predict the teacher's internal representations from a more corrupted input, effectively integrating self-supervised representation alignment into distribution matching. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SF$^2$ effectively mitigates temporal flickering and consistently improves both spatial fidelity and motion quality. Furthermore, the proposed mechanism is architecture-agnostic - seamlessly supporting both bidirectional and causal models - and requires no external feature extractors, introducing minimal computational overhead.

2610.34092.tldr: Leta refines few-step autoregressive video students by directly regressing the teacher-student denoising residual (ScoreDelta) and learning a next-chunk credit signal from teacher-residual VJPs (FutureCredit). It gains +0.9 VBench and +0.66 VideoAlign over DMD in controlled Wan experiments.
2610.34092.why: It targets few-step distillation for autoregressive video diffusion, which bears directly on efficient video DiT inference and long-horizon world-model generation, and it addresses a credit-assignment gap across chunks.
2610.34092.reason: Few-step distillation for autoregressive video diffusion, a core efficiency topic
2610.34092.qn: Neat idea with some theory, but small gains and limited evidence.
2610.34092.abs: Few-step distillation for autoregressive (AR) video generation commonly first initializes an AR student and then refines it with distribution matching distillation (DMD). This refinement process faces two challenges. First, although initialization already yields a reasonably capable student, DMD obtains the refinement direction indirectly by estimating the full student score before forming the teacher-student correction. Second, detached-history training prevents the generator from assigning credit to a current chunk for its influence on subsequent chunks. We introduce Leta, a few-step distillation framework that addresses these challenges with ScoreDelta and FutureCredit. ScoreDelta directly estimates the teacher-student correction from denoising residuals, while FutureCredit learns an auxiliary cross-chunk update signal from vector-Jacobian products (VJPs) of next-chunk teacher residuals. Leta combines these signals into a joint teacher-guided update field in a single forward pass during generator updates. Teacher evaluations and credit VJPs are used only for estimator training. For ScoreDelta, we establish population equivalence to score-difference estimation and a conditional approximation advantage under limited capacity in a fixed-feature linear model. In our controlled experiments, Leta improves over DMD by 0.9 points on VBench and 0.66 on VideoAlign. This advantage persists at a higher generator update frequency (a generator-to-estimator update ratio of G:E=1:1), where Leta improves over DMD by 1.6 on VBench and 0.35 on VideoAlign. Project page: https://scdzx.github.io/Leta/.

2610.33169.tldr: World-in-Context encodes view, action and camera controls as tokens in a video DiT's shared self-attention (in-context conditioning), plus IT-RoPE for control-aware temporal positions. The 5B model matches 22B EchoWM on WBench navigation (81.5 vs 81.6) and reaches 93.8% view-switching success.
2610.33169.why: Directly relevant to camera-controlled video world models on DiTs; in-context control tokens and a control-aware RoPE are a transferable conditioning design versus AdaLN-style pathways.
2610.33169.reason: Interactive video world model with view, action, and camera control tokens
2610.33169.qn: Sensible unified conditioning with strong headline numbers, but in-context conditioning is not novel and evidence is thin.
2610.33169.abs: Interactive video world models require coordinated control over viewing perspectives, character actions, and camera motion. Existing methods typically leave view modes implicit in text captions, conflate action with camera motion, and inject controls through fragmented architectural pathways that capture interdependencies only indirectly. In this work, we present World-in-Context, an interactive world modeling framework powered by In-Context Conditioning (ICC). Rather than relying on specialized conditioning pathways, World-in-Context unifies view, action, and camera controls into explicit tokens contextualized directly within a shared self-attention space. Our formulation reveals that (i) explicit view tokens disentangle conflicting dynamics and unlock emergent view switching from single-view data, while (ii) action and camera inputs play complementary roles in governing local responsiveness and global stability. To preserve temporal continuity across execution intervals, we further introduce Interaction-Transport RoPE (IT-RoPE), parameterizing temporal attention with accumulated control transitions. On WBench, World-in-Context-5B achieves navigation performance on par with 22B EchoWM ($81.5$ vs. $81.6$) and attains a $93.8\%$ perspective-switching success rate, substantially outperforming existing 5B baselines ($18.8\%$). Controlled analyses further demonstrate compounding advantages of World-in-Context under richer conditioning mixtures, favorable data efficiency, and natural applicability to causal rollouts.

2610.33135.tldr: WorldCast renders a depth-backprojected point cloud along large-angle camera trajectories for geometric guidance, and adds Geometry-Aligned Memory Attention to inject multi-view character anchor features. It also introduces CLACT, a dataset of 80k rendered samples with a 42-scene benchmark.
2610.33135.why: Directly relevant to camera-controlled video diffusion with 3D consistency: point-cloud-rendering conditioning plus pose-aligned memory retrieval for unseen regions under large viewpoint changes.
2610.33135.reason: Camera-controlled character video generation with 3D point cloud guidance and large-angle views
2610.33135.qn: Sensible combination and new dataset, but incremental; evaluation is small (42 scenes) and unclear from intro.
2610.33135.abs: Precise camera control is essential for cinematic character video generation, yet existing methods struggle to follow large-angle trajectories with combined rotation, translation, and radius variation from arbitrary initial azimuths. Such viewpoint changes also reveal character regions unseen in the initial frame, causing geometric distortions, appearance degradation, and identity drift. To systematically study these coupled challenges, we introduce CLACT, a large-scale Character-centric dataset and benchmark covering diverse Large-Angle Camera Trajectories, with accurate camera geometry and multi-view character observations for training and evaluation. We further propose WorldCast, a framework for world-consistent character video generation under diverse large-angle camera motions. Importantly, $d=\dim(\theta)$, the dimension of the parameter vector $\theta$, depends on the fineness of the tessellation rather than on the data resolution. Despite this compact parameterization, CPAB optimization has long been hindered by the tight coupling between trajectory integration and gradient computation with respect to $\theta$. By separating integration from parameter-space projection, our method reduces gradient computation complexity from $\mathcal{O}(dTN)$ to $\mathcal{O}(TN+dC)$, where $T$ is the number of integration steps, $N$ is the number of transformed points, and $C$ is the number of tessellation cells. This reformulation yields speedups of up to four orders of magnitude (e.g., $\approx 10^4\times$ in 2D), substantial memory savings (e.g., $\approx 500\times$ reduction in peak GPU memory usage in 2D), and dramatically higher expressiveness. This makes fine-tessellation CPAB practical in 2D and 3D for the first time, enabling highly expressive parametric diffeomorphisms.

The framework first uses image-based geometric registration to align observations from different viewpoints into a shared structural reference, then applies morphology-aware instantiation to assign physically interpretable crack identities, and finally performs temporal mapping in the unified view to distinguish newly developed growth from existing crack segments. To enable evaluation, a temporally annotated dataset was established and used, covering three representative cracking scenarios: single dominant crack propagation, mixed-mode branching, and multiple-crack interaction, with pixel-level masks and cross-time instance labels. Experimental results show that the proposed framework can establish loose cross-view identity correspondence under changing viewpoints, while strict spatial overlap and growth localization remain limited by early micro-crack segmentability and projection drift, highlighting directions for future crack-monitoring research.

2610.34879.abs: Document layout analysis (DLA) faces a long-standing dilemma: existing methods either capture rich local details at prohibitive computational cost (e.g., Transformer-based approaches with quadratic complexity) or achieve efficient global modeling but sacrifice fine-grained structural awareness (e.g., state-space models). This trade-off hinders deployment in resource-constrained scenarios. We present LayoutMamba, a hybrid framework that synergistically combines sparse-attention Transformers for localized feature extraction (O(n) complexity) and the recurrent state-space mechanism of Mamba for dilution-free long-range dependency modeling across the 2D document canvas. Our two-stage paradigm first uses a lightweight Transformer encoder to hierarchically distill salient local semantics; second, Mamba propagates global contextual dependencies without attention dilution, enabling precise, efficient, and scalable layout understanding. We further identify a critical yet overlooked issue in existing DLA benchmarks: the inherent low-overlap distribution bias of layout objects, which we mitigate through a novel Geometric Overlap Penalty Loss (GOPLoss), a dual-optimization objective that minimizes redundant bounding box overlaps and encourages geometrically consistent predictions. Extensive experiments on PubLayNet and D4LA show that LayoutMamba surpasses state-of-the-art AP on PubLayNet with 8x fewer parameters and maintains leading performance on D4LA, ranking top-3 among published methods, achieving an unprecedented balance between accuracy, efficiency, and scalability. Our work pioneers a cognition-inspired paradigm for document analysis, advancing practical deployment in edge computing and resource-limited environments.

2610.34795.reason: Urban twin and agent survey; tangential to core interests
2610.34795.qn: Survey with system blueprint; no quantitative evidence
2610.34795.abs: Cities must coordinate domains like infrastructure, mobility, environmental management, emergency response, and public services as conditions evolve. An urban Spatio-Temporal Intelligence (STI) system helps the city monitor citywide states, analyze problems, plan and execute interventions, and adapt through feedback, making urban governance more timely, effective, and transparent. Recent urban twinning and agentic AI techniques provide foundations for such systems. From a twin-agent perspective, this survey takes a system-level view of how these disparate techniques can be coherently integrated into an urban STI system. Specifically, we review how the twin reconstructs and represents a persistent, information-enriched urban environment, and how the agent understands the twin via interfaces, reasons over it, acts reliably, and continuously evolves with the city. Built upon this synthesis, we summarize a two-loop blueprint, where an inner agent loop for grounding, reasoning, and verification, and an outer system loop linking data, twin, agentic action, feedback, and update. We then use this to structure an STI research agenda and show how a shared prototype supports diverse urban domains.

2610.33810.reason: Open-ended image editing; not core to 3D or video diffusion
2610.33810.qn: Two-stage editing framework with relative gains but few method details
2610.33810.abs: Open-ended image-editing requests, such as ``decorate this room,'' admit multiple valid realizations. Direct sampling may produce ungrounded variation, whereas explicit diversity prompting often produces superficial differences. We study how to ground these requests without prematurely eliminating their legitimate ambiguity. We introduce a two-stage framework that first identifies diverse, feasible edit scopes and then realizes them as executable edit instructions. Across 300 open-ended image-editing tasks, our approach achieves 24.6% higher mean semantic dispersion and 17.1% higher mean groundedness than direct diversity prompting, while producing more valid and distinct realizations. These results show that structuring feasible edit directions before realization supports more useful grounded exploration.

2610.33062.reason: Unified multimodal generation/understanding; loosely related to generation
2610.33062.qn: Latent visual reasoning in unified models; evidence limited to seven tasks
2610.33062.abs: Unified large multimodal models (ULMMs) are able to perform visual reasoning through interleaved text-image generation, but generating explicit intermediate images incurs significant computational overhead. While visual latent reasoning addresses this, most existing methods rely on vision-language models (VLMs) incapable of visual generation. We propose Oddin, a novel framework enabling latent visual reasoning in ULMMs. Oddin replaces intermediate images with compact latent tokens processed entirely by the understanding branch, reserving the generation branch for the final output image. We train the model via offline self-distillation with three objectives, final image generation losses, text distillation losses, and cross-entropy losses for special tokens. Oddin surpasses interleaved generation baselines and closed-source VLMs on average across seven VBVR-Pro visual reasoning tasks. Qualitative analysis reveals that latent tokens attend to relevant regions in an input image, demonstrating that ULMMs can perform complex visual reasoning without generating intermediate images.

2610.33019.reason: Agent memory for multimodal models; not in core 3D/video diffusion topics
2610.33019.qn: Reasonable dual-memory idea; evaluation details vague, gains modest
2610.33019.abs: As multimodal agents engage in sustained interactions, long-term memory serves two distinct but complementary functions: fine-grained evidence recall and internalized interpretation for global understanding. Although episodic and latent memory address these demands through explicit historical records and internalized experience, neither paradigm alone can accommodate the diverse memory affinities across tasks, owing to limitations in episodic evidence coverage and integration, and in latent factual grounding. To bridge this divide, we propose a dual-memory framework, unifying a model-native latent memory as an intuitive prior with a multi-indexed episodic memory for exact evidence reconstruction via retrieval-conditioned joint alignment. At inference, the framework adaptively composes these memories through a training-free routing mechanism driven by Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD) sensitivity and confidence proxies for query-dependent memory affinity. Extensive evaluations across multimodal benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, outperforming single-paradigm baselines overall (+4.67\% over vanilla Episodic), with further analysis highlighting episodic strengths in evidence-localized tasks and latent contributions to integrating dispersed information and compensating for imperfect retrieval.
